meaning: A sweet, reproachful complaint for not visiting or calling.
cultural_vibe: Rooted in Marwari hospitality, 'Olbho' captures the gentle grievance of elders missing their loved ones.
dialogue_marwari: अरे बन्ना! दो महिना होइग्या, थाने कदै याद ई कोनी आई? थारो ओळभो करणो पड़सी अब तो!
dialogue_english: Hey dear! It's been two months, didn't you even remember us? Now we must lodge a sweet complaint (olbho) against you!
family_prompt: Who in the family do you owe an 'olbho' to for not calling this week? Tag them below!

theme: Kitchen, Food & Street Snacks (Ransoi, Chatkara & Mitthan)
meaning: Traditional sweet broken-wheat dessert cooked with ghee, jaggery, and dry fruits.
cultural_vibe: The ultimate symbol of auspicious beginnings and celebrations in Marwari homes, served during festivals and family milestones.
dialogue_marwari: बेटा, आज शुभ काम है, रसोई में गरमा-गरम लापसी और सीरा बना लीज्यो!
dialogue_english: Son, today is an auspicious occasion, do prepare hot laapsi and sheera in the kitchen!
family_prompt: Who in our family makes the best, most ghee-dripping Laapsi? Share your memories!

theme: Kitchen, Food & Street Snacks (Ransoi, Chatkara & Mitthan)
meaning: Thick, crisp pearl millet (bajra) flatbread served generously with white butter.
cultural_vibe: The undisputed king of Marwari winter tables, traditionally paired with lasun ki chutney and fresh white butter to keep the desert chill at bay.
dialogue_marwari: अरे छोरा, बाजरे को गरम सोगरो ल्याऊं के ऊपर देसी घी चूपड़'र?
dialogue_english: Hey son, shall I bring a hot bajra sogro drenched in homemade ghee?
family_prompt: Who in our family makes the crispiest sogro, and do you prefer it with gur (jaggery) or lehsun ki chutney?

theme: Vintage Artifacts & Sunday Wisdom (Ghar Ri Cheezan & Gyan)
meaning: Traditional cylindrical amulet worn as a pendant by Rajasthani women.
cultural_vibe: A treasured heirloom passed down generations, symbolizing heritage protection, auspiciousness, and classic Marwari craftsmanship.
dialogue_marwari: दादी: बेटा, ई संदूक खोलर म्हारो पुराणो चाँदी रो मांदळियो काढ तो सही, आज रविवार है तो साफ-सफाई कर लूँ।
dialogue_english: Grandmother: Son, open this chest and take out my old silver Mandaliyo, since it's Sunday I want to clean it up.
family_prompt: Does anyone in our family still have or wear an old silver Mandaliyo or heirloom piece from our ancestral home?

meaning: A false cloud or mirage of rain that disappears without showering.
cultural_vibe: Captures the hopeful yet testing relationship Marwaris have with fickle desert monsoon clouds.
dialogue_marwari: आज तो आकाश में घणी बदळियां छाई है, पण इण मूळ धूप में तौ लागे 'झूठो मेह' ही निकळसी।
dialogue_english: Today the sky is full of clouds, but in this scorching heat, it feels like it's just a false rain cloud.
family_prompt: Have you ever experienced a desert mirage or a false rain cloud during your visits to Rajasthan?

meaning: A cool, refreshing breeze that blows during the desert evening.
cultural_vibe: Captures the sudden relief and joy brought by the gentle evening wind after a scorching Thar summer day.
dialogue_marwari: अरे छोरा, बारै ओसरे जाइजे, कत्तौ सारौ झिझवा चल रयौ है!
dialogue_english: Hey child, go out to the verandah, such a lovely evening breeze is blowing!
family_prompt: Do you remember the cool desert breeze during your summer visits to Rajasthan?

meaning: The scorching heat wave unique to the Thar Desert.
cultural_vibe: Captures the intense summer winds of Marwar that teach resilience and the art of staying indoors during peak afternoons.
dialogue_marwari: अरे छोरा, बळती दुपहरी बा'र मत जाइज्यो, कठेई 'लू री लपेट' में कोनी आ जाव।
dialogue_english: Hey child, don't go outside in the blazing afternoon, lest you get caught in the hot desert wind.
family_prompt: What is the highest temperature you have ever experienced, and how do you beat the heat like a true Marwari?

meaning: Masters of the sand dunes, referring to the majestic camel.
cultural_vibe: An affectionate and respectful ode to the camel, the indispensable lifeline of the Thar Desert.
dialogue_marwari: दादूजी: देख बेटा, धोरां रा धणी बिना मरुधरे री जीवनशैली अधूरी है।
dialogue_english: Grandfather: Look son, without the masters of the dunes, life in our desert land is incomplete.
family_prompt: Have you ever seen a camel in person during your visits to Rajasthan? Share your best memory!

meaning: A gentle, affectionate complaint or reminder of emotional grievance.
cultural_vibe: Olbho is uniquely Marwari—not quite a complaint, but a soft emotional nudge used by elders when you haven't called or visited in a while, wrapped in deep love.
dialogue_marwari: दादी: 'बेटे, घणादिना सूं फोन कोनी आयो, बसम् थारो ओळभो ही रेई ग्यो।'
dialogue_english: Grandmother: 'Son, you haven't called in days, now all I am left with is your gentle complaint.'
family_prompt: Who in the family gives you the sweetest 'olbho' when you forget to call? Tag them below!
